title: Principal multiplication data from a schematically dense generic open
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative integral domain and $B$ a commutative finite type $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $K$ be the fraction field of $A$, the localization at all nonzero elements, and put $B_K=B\otimes_A K$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Write $X=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $X_K=\operatorname{Spec}B_K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be an open subscheme, and $U_K$ its inverse image under the canonical projection $X_K\to X$. Suppose the open inclusion $j_K:U_K\hookrightarrow X_K$ induces an injective map of sheaves $\mathcal O_{X_K}\to(j_K)_*\mathcal O_{U_K}$. There exist $m\geq0$ and $g_1,\ldots,g_m\in B$ such that $D(g_i)\subseteq U$ for every $i$, $U_K=\bigcup_{i=1}^mD(g_i\otimes1)$, and the map $\mu_K:B_K\to B_K^{\oplus m}$, $b\mapsto((g_i\otimes1)b)_i$, is injective. Here $D(g)=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}B:g\notin\mathfrak p\}$, and the union and tuple for $m=0$ are empty. No quasi-compactness of $U$ is assumed.

proof.text: Choose finite $A$-algebra generators $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ of $B$ using [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. They give $K$-algebra generators $t_i\otimes1$ of $B_K$: by [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors, and if $b=P(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$ then $b\otimes k=kP_K(t_1\otimes1,\ldots,t_r\otimes1)$, where $P_K$ maps each coefficient of $P$ into $K$. Every ideal of the field $K$ is either zero or, by multiplying a nonzero element by its inverse, the unit ideal; hence $K$ is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] to $K\to B_K$ to conclude that $B_K$ is Noetherian.

The one-chart affine covering of $X_K=\operatorname{Spec}B_K$ makes it locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth], since its section ring is $B_K$. It is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so it is a Noetherian scheme. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] to the open $U_K\subseteq X_K$. In particular, $U_K$ is quasi-compact: every open covering of its underlying space has a finite subcover.

Let $G=\{g\in B:D(g)\subseteq U\}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open](i), $U=\bigcup_{g\in G}D(g)$. Under the canonical map $p:X_K\to X$, a prime $\mathfrak q\subset B_K$ maps to the inverse image prime in $B$, so $p(\mathfrak q)\in D(g)$ if and only if $g\otimes1\notin\mathfrak q$. Thus $p^{-1}D(g)=D(g\otimes1)$, and inverse images of the displayed union give $U_K=\bigcup_{g\in G}D(g\otimes1)$. These are open by the same basis statement applied to $B_K$. Choose a finite subcover by Step 2 and enumerate its functions as $g_1,\ldots,g_m$. Each still belongs to $G$, so $D(g_i)\subseteq U$. If $U_K$ is empty, choose the empty subcover and $m=0$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-affine-schematic-density-criterion] with ring $B_K$, integer $m$, and functions $f_i=g_i\otimes1$. Step 3 identifies the union of its principal opens with $U_K$, so its open immersion is precisely $j_K$ and its sheaf-injectivity hypothesis is the one assumed here. Its equivalent multiplication condition is injectivity of $b\mapsto((g_i\otimes1)b)_i$, exactly $\mu_K$. The criterion permits $m=0$; then injectivity says $B_K=0$, as is also forced by the assumed sheaf injection when $U_K$ is empty.
